done_when: Forge's Codex trust check accepts a project inside a trusted folder whenever Codex itself trusts it, and asks only when Codex would ask

known.title: Trust lookup can authorize turns that Codex treats as untrusted
Not done: Forge's Codex trust check accepts a project inside a trusted folder whenever Codex trusts it, and asks only when Codex would ask
Standard: each commit leaves the build working

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 3, Harm 4
Raise: Security. `_codex_trust` reads only the user's `config.toml`, but Codex also [overlays managed configuration before deciding trust](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.159.2/codex-rs/config/src/loader/project_discovery.rs#L293-L343). If the user file trusts a project and managed configuration marks it untrusted, Forge starts a turn whose project hooks Codex skips. A trusted project-root entry supplied by managed configuration produces the opposite mismatch: Forge asks when Codex would not. On Windows, `_codex_keys` at line 45 also uses Unicode `lower()`, while [Codex lowercases ASCII only](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.159.2/codex-rs/config/src/loader/mod.rs#L1302-L1322); differently cased non-ASCII path keys can therefore be trusted by Forge but not Codex. The named tests cover user-file entries with ASCII paths, leaving these mismatches undetected.

why: Forge says Codex does not trust a project that sits inside a folder Codex already trusts
